Matched-profile results

Zig, C, C++, Go and Rust use 48 kHz PCM24 WAV or libmp3lame 320 kbps MP3. All use FFmpeg DSP. Zig remains the comparison denominator despite its listed safety failures.

Cases have equal weight. A clear speed observation requires at least 5% difference and disjoint observed ranges. Overlapping variation counts as a tie.

Node profile comparison

Node uses 44.1 kHz float WAV and lamejs MP3. Its DSP, encoder, sample count and fsync behavior differ. Its time and memory ratios below describe the observed export; they are excluded from the matched-workload aggregate.

Node geometric mean Zig / Node time: 0.197. Median sampled RSS / Zig: 9.392.

Method and limits

192 cases cross 20 ms, 1 s, 60 s, 600 s, 2 × 30 s and 16 × 3.75 s inputs; WAV/MP3 input and output; ratios 0.5/1/1.255/2; fresh/overwrite publication. One untimed warmup precedes seven rotated speed runs and a separate sampled memory pass. Startup through final publication and process exit is timed.

RSS sums simultaneously sampled wrapper and child resident memory, including validators. The sampler waits 2 ms after each scan and records actual cadence. Process reads within a scan are not atomic; brief peaks may be missed and shared mappings may be counted more than once. It is neither wrapper-only RSS nor the sum of unrelated per-process maxima. Memory passes do not enter speed medians.

Other sessions and a busy single-core Python process remained active. Host load and swap were recorded. Filesystem caches were not purged; separate first-launch measurements do not establish disk-cold latency. This is macOS arm64 evidence, with no physical listening or second-device access claim.
